title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 20
paragraphs: For in fact the Euboeans, disregarding the oracle of Bakis as if it had no meaning, had neither carried anything out of their land nor laid in any provisions with a view to a war coming upon them, and by their behavior they had brought trouble on themselves. For the oracle of Bakis concerning these matters runs as follows:
“Mark, when a man — a barbarian — shall yoke the sea with papyrus, then plan to remove the loud-bleating goats from Euboea.”
In the evils now upon them, or soon to be expected, they had good cause to regret having paid no attention to these lines.
